# Performance

spec

The target is a docc check and a docc build on 1000 documents in under 300 ms each. It is measured with a generated project of 1000 files with 5 to 20 KB of Russian text each (about 7 MB), with links, a parent tree and a kind schema.

On Linux (Intel Core i7-1165G7) the whole check takes about 0.25 seconds: loading 20 ms, rules and the link hashes of `docc.lock` 140 ms, rendering 45 ms and comparing the output folder 10 ms; a build takes the same.

The measurement is repeatable with DOCC_SCALE set to 1 and the command cargo test --release --test scale -- --nocapture. Windows with a virus scanner and macOS have not been measured.

## History

The first measurement was 1.66 seconds. The word lists were matched with case-insensitive regular expressions, which took most of the time; a lower-cased search with word boundary checks brought it to 0.31 seconds. Matching in NFC and the hashes of `docc.lock` raised it to 1.58 seconds; an NFC test that skips the norm tables for Cyrillic and Latin text, one lower-cased copy shared by the word lists and one hash per link target brought it to 0.67 seconds. The rewrite in Rust brought check and build to 0.25 seconds.
